claim: Adding palbociclib to letrozole improves overall survival in HR-positive advanced breast cancer
gold_rationale: Palbociclib + letrozole is FDA/EMA-approved on the basis of a large, statistically significant PROGRESSION-FREE SURVIVAL benefit (PALOMA-2, Finn NEJM 2016, PFS HR 0.58) — but PFS is a surrogate, not overall survival. The protocol-specified secondary OS endpoint of the same pivotal trial was formally NEGATIVE: PALOMA-2 final OS (Slamon/Finn JCO 2024) gave HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.78-1.18), one-sided P=.34; median 53.9 vs 51.2 months — no significant OS improvement (imbalance-corrected sensitivity HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.76-1.12, remained non-significant). The second palbociclib pivotal trial, PALOMA-3 (palbociclib + fulvestrant, Turner NEJM 2018), also did not meet statistical significance for OS in the ITT population (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.64-1.03, P=.09), though direction favored palbociclib. By explicit contrast, ribociclib + letrozole (MONALEESA-2, Hortobagyi NEJM 2022) DID show a significant OS benefit (HR 0.76, P=.008); the PALOMA-2 JCO authors themselves state 'Currently, only ribociclib has shown a statistically significant improvement in OS in this setting.' Therefore the specific claim — that adding PALBOCICLIB to letrozole improves OS — is contradicted by its own pivotal randomized OS analysis and is Not Supported at the level of statistical significance, despite a clear PFS benefit and a numerically favorable but non-significant OS point estimate.
population: HR+/HER2- advanced (metastatic) breast cancer, first-line (PALOMA-2) or endocrine-pretreated (PALOMA-3)

baseline.text: Yes. Palbociclib is a CDK4/6 inhibitor that, added to letrozole, substantially improves outcomes in HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. The PALOMA-2 trial showed palbociclib plus letrozole roughly doubled progression-free survival (about 25 vs 14 months) versus letrozole alone, and this combination is a standard first-line therapy expected to extend overall survival in these patients.

rows.citation: Finn RS, Martin M, Rugo HS, et al. Palbociclib and Letrozole in Advanced Breast Cancer (PALOMA-2). N Engl J Med. 2016;375(20):1925-1936. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1607303
rows.integrity_note: Pivotal phase 3, double-blind, 2:1 randomization, N=666. Primary endpoint (PFS) met; funded by Pfizer. Verified against PubMed metadata + abstract; article types include 'Randomized Controlled Trial, Clinical Trial, Phase III'; NOT retracted.
rows.finding: PALOMA-2 pivotal trial: primary endpoint was PROGRESSION-FREE SURVIVAL (a surrogate), median 24.8 vs 14.5 months (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.46-0.72, P<0.001). OS was only a secondary endpoint and not reported as significant here. Direction on the CLAIMED outcome (OS) = 0 because this report establishes the PFS surrogate benefit, not an OS benefit.

rows.citation: Slamon DJ, Dieras V, Rugo HS, ... Finn RS. Overall Survival With Palbociclib Plus Letrozole in Advanced Breast Cancer (PALOMA-2 final OS). J Clin Oncol. 2024;42(9):994-1000. DOI:10.1200/JCO.23.00137
rows.integrity_note: Protocol-specified final OS analysis of the pivotal PALOMA-2 RCT; 405 deaths (273/444 palbociclib arm vs 132/222 placebo, confirmed in JCO text), median follow-up 90.1 months. Imbalance in unknown survival status (13.3% vs 21.2%) noted; sensitivity analysis with recovered data also non-significant. Verified against PubMed + JCO/PMC full text.
rows.finding: PIVOTAL NEGATIVE OS RESULT: median OS 53.9 vs 51.2 months, HR 0.96 (95% CI 0.78-1.18), stratified one-sided P=.34. With recovered survival data HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.76-1.12), one-sided P=.21. Authors: 'OS was not significantly improved with palbociclib plus letrozole.' Directly contradicts the claim on the exact claimed outcome and population.

rows.citation: Turner NC, Slamon DJ, Ro J, et al. Overall Survival with Palbociclib and Fulvestrant in Advanced Breast Cancer (PALOMA-3). N Engl J Med. 2018;379(20):1926-1936. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa1810527
rows.integrity_note: Phase 3 RCT, palbociclib+FULVESTRANT (not letrozole) in endocrine-pretreated HR+/HER2- ABC; 521 randomized 2:1 (n_int=347 palbociclib). OS prespecified secondary; ITT result non-significant. Verified against PubMed + NEJM abstract; NOT retracted.
rows.finding: PALOMA-3: ITT median OS 34.9 vs 28.0 months, HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.64-1.03), P=.09 — favorable direction but NOT statistically significant. Different endocrine partner (fulvestrant) and pretreated population; scored direction 0 (null on formal significance).

rows.citation: Hortobagyi GN, Stemmer SM, Burris HA, et al. Overall Survival with Ribociclib plus Letrozole in Advanced Breast Cancer (MONALEESA-2 final OS). N Engl J Med. 2022;386(10):942-950. DOI:10.1056/NEJMoa2114663
rows.integrity_note: Phase 3 RCT of a DIFFERENT CDK4/6 inhibitor (RIBOCICLIB) + letrozole, same population/partner; 334 per arm, hierarchical testing preserved validity. Verified against PubMed + NEJM full text. Direction corrected from -1 to 0: because this trial does not test palbociclib, a positive ribociclib OS result cannot directly contradict the palbociclib-specific claim — it is class-contrast/drug-specificity context (null with respect to the claimed intervention), not evidence against palbociclib.
rows.finding: Contrast trial: ribociclib+letrozole gave significant OS benefit, median 63.9 vs 51.4 months, HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.63-0.93), two-sided P=.008. Demonstrates drug-SPECIFICITY: only ribociclib (not palbociclib) has shown a statistically significant first-line OS benefit. Included as context; does not directly test the palbociclib claim, hence direction 0 (not -1).
